title.rendered: He Makes Me Lie Down: The Shepherd Who Insists on Rest | Living from Rest, Day 5

excerpt.rendered: Psalm 23 says the Shepherd makes His sheep lie down in green pastures. Day 5 of Living from Rest explores why God sometimes insists on the pause.

content.rendered:
Sheep rarely lie down on their own. The shepherd knows this. So he engineers the field, the water, the quiet, until the restless animal finally bends its knees. That shepherd is the Lord.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, November 5, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 5

Today’s Scripture

“The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me to lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside the still waters. He restores my soul; He leads me in the paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.”
Psalm 23:1-3 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Psalm 23 is the most quoted chapter in the Bible for a reason. It is comfort set to music. But look again at verse 2. “He makes me to lie down in green pastures.” Makes. Not invites. Not suggests. Makes. The Hebrew word carries the sense of causing, bringing about. The Good Shepherd engineers the circumstances until the sheep finally rests.

Psalm 23:2, in the NKJV, says, “He makes me to lie down in green pastures.” The AMPC says, “He makes me lie down in [fresh, tender] green pastures; He leads me beside the still and restful waters.” The TPT says, “He offers a resting place for me in his luxurious love. His tracks take me to an oasis of peace near the quiet brook of bliss.”

Phillip Keller, a pastor who had worked as a shepherd before he preached, said four things must be true before a sheep will lie down. The sheep must be free from fear; free from friction with other sheep; free from flies and pests; free from hunger. The shepherd works on each of those. He drives off predators. He breaks up quarrels. He treats the pests. He feeds the flock. Only then do the sheep lie down. The Good Shepherd does the same for us. Our capacity to rest is often downstream of His unseen work on the field.

There are seasons when God slows us. We call it an illness, a redundancy, a closed door, a disrupted plan. We often read those seasons as failure. Psalm 23 invites a different reading. Could this be the shepherd making you lie down? Could this be the engineering of a rest you would not have taken otherwise? Not every slowdown is a judgment. Some are mercies. He is restoring your soul, in a pasture you did not choose.

If life is loud this morning, know this: the Shepherd knows how to find a quiet brook even inside a storm. Still waters are not always external; sometimes they are a settled inner life next to a chaotic outer one. He is leading you there. Let Him lead. Lie down. Trust the pasture. The One who brought you to it does not waste a single blade of grass.

How the Shepherd Builds Rest

He removes fear. You are not alone; He is with you, and that changes the field.

He engineers quiet. He will slow you if needed, so your soul can be restored.

He restores before He leads. You are poured back into before you are sent out again.

Declaration

The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. I trust the pasture He has placed me in. I trust the pace He has set for me. I will not resist the rest He is building into my life. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
